title: Transformer Architecture — Encoder, Decoder, or Both
key_insight: Encoders use bidirectional attention over available input. Decoder-only models use causal attention. Encoder-decoder models let a generating decoder also attend to encoded source text.
body:
## Encoder, Decoder, or Both

One task understands a complete sentence; another generates the next token without seeing the future. They need different attention rules.

Encoders use bidirectional attention over available input. Decoder-only models use causal attention. Encoder-decoder models let a generating decoder also attend to encoded source text.

Choose the layout for the task rather than treating every transformer as identical. Modern chat models are commonly decoder-only.
common_mistakes: A transformer contains attention and nothing else.
Decoder generation should read future unseen tokens.
A key-value cache makes memory use shrink as context grows.
mini_exercise: Draw “Encoder, Decoder, or Both” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Transformers are the architecture behind modern language models and many vision and multimodal systems.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Encoder, Decoder, or Both,” explain Transformer Architecture without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
